about: The owner of the orchestration_sign_in tool and its result texts (docs/vm-browser-bridge.md, section 7). The Python server reads this file. The Rust catalog (runtime-services account_worker/preparation-resources.json) and the Rust results (runtime-services sign_in.rs) are checked against it.

tool.name: orchestration_sign_in
tool.description: Show the person a sign-in card for a link that they must open to sign in or approve access: an OAuth, OpenID Connect, SSO or SAML sign-in page, a device code page, or the loopback sign-in page of a command. After the person approves the card, the link opens in the person's own browser on their Mac or phone, and the sign-in result returns to the command. Use this tool for every such link that a command prints or that you must give to the person. Do not open the link in another way, and do not give it in a message as the only way to open it. Keep the sign-in command running while the person signs in. A repeated call with the same link returns the same card.

submitSecondsAbout: The longest wait, in seconds, for the browser bridge to queue a link. A loopback start page costs one first hop of at most 5 seconds.
messageAgeSecondsAbout: The oldest completed agent message, in seconds, whose sign-in links get cards. It is the lifetime of a bridge request, so a message that history recovery writes again makes no card.

results.pending: Studio shows the person a sign-in card for {host}. After the approval, the link opens in the person's own browser. Keep the sign-in command running and wait for it.
results.approved: The person approved the sign-in at {host}. Keep the sign-in command running: the result goes to it.
results.opened: The person opened the page at {host}. Keep the sign-in command running until it ends.
results.declined: The person declined to open {host}. Do not give this link again unless the person asks for it.
results.closed: The sign-in request for {host} has ended. Run the sign-in command again if it still needs a sign-in.
results.unsupported: The browser bridge of this chat is older than this tool. Run "$BROWSER" with the link in the chat's shell instead; in the Linux VM, run studio-browser with the link.

unsupportedMessage: The browser method is not supported
unsupportedMessageAbout: The refusal of a bridge from before browser.submit (browser_bridge.py and browser_host.rs, method call).
